PPOL 1110.title: Public Policy in Cases
PPOL 1110.description: This course aims to equip students with conceptual and theoretical abilities that are essential for understanding the complex but fascinating world of public policy. Theoretical knowledge will be illustrated through 13 real-world policy cases from Asia, Africa, and North America, covering a wide range of areas including health care, poverty alleviation, rural development, technology innovation, and crisis management. Students will engage the class through dynamic co-production of knowledge. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to comprehend and analyze the dynamics of public policy in a professional way and will also develop higher-order capabilities of solving contemporary policy problems.
cilos: Identify and define key terms, concepts, approaches, and frameworks concerning public policy
Classify, infer and explain important structures and interactions among key components of policy systems, such as policy actors, policy environment, and policy instruments
Exemplify, summarize and paraphrase key theories and frameworks of the policy process and identify and apply areas of potential improvement
Differentiate, distinguish and analyze the political system, policy approach, and socioeconomic dynamics of different types of societies around the world

PPOL 1120.title: Public Policy for a Healthy Society
PPOL 1120.description: This course aims to introduce students from all disciplines to fundamental public policy concepts through the lens of public health and sustainable societies. This course will examine how governments, organisations, and communities develop, implement, and evaluate policies that promote health and wellbeing. The course emphasizes interdisciplinary learning by connecting public policy concepts with societal health challenges that affect daily life, from pandemic responses to mental health initiatives. Through case studies, debates, group discussions, and practical exercises, students will develop critical thinking skills to analyse complex policy problems, assess evidence-based solutions, and appreciate the ethical dimensions of public policy. This course's mission is to provide well-rounded knowledge and skills that nurture responsible, ethical, and compassionate professionals capable of contributing meaningfully to society.
cilos: Analyze and evaluate public policies using established frameworks, demonstrating understanding of the policy cycle, stakeholder dynamics, and policy instruments in health-related contexts
Critically examine the ethical dimensions of public policy decisions, considering issues of equity, individual liberty, and collective responsibility in health policy contexts

Synthesise interdisciplinary knowledge by connecting public policy concepts with health and medical sciences, economics, behavioural science, and other relevant fields to understand multifaceted policy challenges
Apply comparative analysis to assess how different jurisdictions and systems approach similar public health challenges, identifying factors that contribute to policy success or failure

Develop evidence-based policy recommendations that consider stakeholder perspectives, implementation challenges, and potential unintended consequences, demonstrating practical application of policy analysis skills
Communicate effectively about complex policy issues to diverse audiences, demonstrating ability to translate technical policy analysis into accessible formats for public engagement

Develop evidence-based policy recommendations that consider stakeholder perspectives, implementation challenges, and potential unintended consequences, demonstrating practical application of policy analysis skills
Communicate effectively about complex policy issues to diverse audiences, demonstrating ability to translate technical policy analysis into accessible formats for public engagement

PPOL 1130.title: Introduction to Global Public Policy Through Film
PPOL 1130.description: This course utilizes award-winning films to introduce students to the most pressing global public policy challenges facing policymakers today. It is divided into six interconnected modules, focusing on the global governance of poverty and inequality, finance and financial crises, taxation and offshore tax dodging, climate change and ecocide, peace and security, and corporate power and accountability, with each module emphasizing the role of disruptive technological advances like generative artificial intelligence, decentralized finance, digitalization and dematerialization of the economy, decarbonization of production, uncrewed and autonomous systems, social media algorithms, and more. Students will be equipped with the necessary skills to analyze these global challenges, assess the opportunities and threats posed by key technologies, and formulate their own solutions. The course will appeal to students pursuing careers in national and international public administrations, consulting and advisory firms, corporate compliance departments, think tanks, civil society organizations, news media outlets, and other relevant bodies.
cilos: Explain the key terms, concepts, mechanisms, structural dynamics, and ideological struggles necessary for a comprehensive understanding of contemporary global public policy challenges
Analyze the roots, impacts, and seeming intractability of contemporary global public policy challenges, and assess the opportunities and threats posed by key disruptive technological advances

Distinguish between the objectives of different state and non-state actors involved in the global governance of contemporary global public policy challenges, the reasons behind their objectives, and the strategies they deploy in their attempts to preserve or change the regulatory and legislative status quo

Evaluate the effectiveness of existing policies, frameworks, reforms, initiatives, campaigns, and other efforts aimed at tackling contemporary global public policy challenges, and the potential effectiveness as well as the technical and political feasibility of more ambitious approaches

Develop essential theoretical, conceptual, critical thinking, analytical, research, and writing skills necessary for the formulation and implementation of comprehensive policy solutions and effective enforcement mechanisms that adequately address contemporary global public policy challenges

PPOL 2000.title: Special Topics in Public Policy
PPOL 2000.description: Selected topics of current interest in public policy studies. The course aims to broaden students' exposure to a broad range of topics within the public policy discipline. The course may be repeated for credit, if the topics studied are different. Graded letter grade or P/F subject to different offerings. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course.
cilos: Have an understanding of many important areas from the Public Policy perspective.
Describe and critique existing approaches to special topics in public policy.
Use effective skills in communication, analysis, information collection and presentation within the team.
Explain the meaning and significance of public policy.
Analyze existing special topics of development to public policy.

PPOL 2110.title: Science, Technology and Society in China
PPOL 2110.description: This course aims to cultivate students’ systematic and critical thinking about science, technology, innovation, and society, especially in light of the transition from traditional China to contemporary China. Differing from the usual courses focusing on this subject, this course will take a social and critical approach, enabling students to understand and analyze the social, political, and cultural preconditions and impacts of scientific and technological development. By the end of the course, students should understand the significance of the social, cultural, and political preconditions underlying scientific and technological innovations and be able to gauge the impact of those innovations. They should also be able to systematically analyze the factors that make innovation significant and use this analysis to critically examine the development of science and technology over the course of China’s history.
cilos: Exemplify and classify the common definitions of science, technology, and innovation as well as the general relationships between science, technology, and society
Describe the driving forces, features, and major achievements in scientific and technological development in ancient and medieval China
Evaluate the sources, importance, and effects of the industrial revolution, especially its importance to global scientific and technological thought
Differentiate and distinguish the ‘divergence’ between the West and China during the scientific and industrial revolutions
Exemplify, analyze and apply the innovation systems conceptual approach to the development of science and technology in China over the various periods of the last century

PPOL 2110.title: Science, Technology and Society in China
PPOL 2110.description: This course aims to cultivate students’ systematic and critical thinking about science, technology, innovation, and society, especially in light of the transition from traditional China to contemporary China. Differing from the usual courses focusing on this subject, this course will take a social and critical approach, enabling students to understand and analyze the social, political, and cultural preconditions and impacts of scientific and technological development.
